findings.message: Criteria 4, 5 and 7 say tests/integration/test_mcp_app_dashboard.py verifies them by running this harness, and Scope in lists the checks it must make. The harness only checks that the step-time span is the second child and that the last row has step-warning. It never checks step-passed on engine_start or *_ok rows, step-failed on engine_stop or *_failed rows, or step-muted on *_start rows. It never checks the engine_start/engine_stop outline paths or the preflight rocket path. It makes none of the dashboard.css checks: `.step-row:disabled { opacity: 1`, the four outcome color rules, no bold on .step-stem, no `margin-left: auto` on .step-time, and .step-text using descriptionForeground. It never checks that a section toggle, a resize pointerup or a drag-and-drop calls clutch_app_ui_state set; only the ▲ click is checked. On polling, it never checks that an overlapping refresh is skipped or that changing to a nonzero refreshSeconds resets the interval at the new period. So these criteria pass whether or not the behavior is there.
findings.paved_road: Add harness assertions: the class on each step row by kind (engine_start → step-passed, engine_stop → step-failed, *_start → step-muted); the icon paths; regexes over dashboard.css for each required CSS rule and for the absent bold and margin-left rules; a set call after a toggle dispatch, a resizer pointerup and a drop; and for polling, a nonzero change that clears the old interval and schedules one at the new ms, plus a second refresh during an in-flight one that makes no extra clutch_app_snapshot call.

findings.message: Criterion 2 and Definition of rejected require that clutch_app_config set keeps unrelated config.yaml keys. The test only checks the returned max_runs and never checks that other keys from VALID are still in the written file, so a set that drops keys would still pass.
findings.paved_road: After the successful set, load config.yaml with yaml.safe_load and assert that the top-level keys from VALID other than scheduler.parallel are still there with their original values.

findings.message: The Refresh seconds handler takes any non-negative number with `Math.max(0, Number(n.value) || 0)`, so 2.5 becomes the polling period. But clutch_app_ui_state merge only accepts an int refreshSeconds, so the server quietly keeps the old value. The dashboard then polls at a period that is never saved, and the preference is lost on reopen, which Definition of rejected forbids.
findings.paved_road: Round the client value to an integer (for example `Math.max(0, Math.round(Number(n.value)) || 0)`) and set `step = 1` on the number input, so the client and server accept the same values.
